content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In mainstream Christian teaching, marriage and the bride are understood as symbols of the covenant union between Christ and the Church: Christ is the bridegroom and the Church (the collective people of God) is his bride. The imagery expresses exclusive covenant loyalty, sacrificial love, purification, and the anticipated consummation of that union at the eschatological 'marriage supper of the Lamb.' This builds on the Old Testament portrayal of Israel as the wife of YHWH, with idolatry depicted as adultery or harlotry.","primary_basis":["Ephesians 5:22-33 (husband/wife as Christ/Church, 'this mystery is great')","Revelation 19:7-9 (marriage supper of the Lamb; the bride has made herself ready)","Revelation 21:2, 9 (New Jerusalem as a bride adorned for her husband; 'the bride, the wife of the Lamb')","Revelation 22:17 ('the Spirit and the bride say, Come')","2 Corinthians 11:2 (Paul betroths the church as a pure virgin to Christ)","John 3:29 (John the Baptist calls Jesus the bridegroom)","Matthew 9:15 / Mark 2:19-20 / Luke 5:34-35 (Jesus as bridegroom)","Matthew 22:1-14 (parable of the wedding banquet)","Matthew 25:1-13 (parable of the ten virgins awaiting the bridegroom)","Hosea 1-3 (Israel as unfaithful wife; God's covenant love)","Isaiah 54:5-6; 62:4-5 ('your Maker is your husband')","Jeremiah 2:2; 3:14, 20 (Israel's bridal devotion and adultery)","Ezekiel 16 and 23 (covenant marriage and unfaithfulness allegories)","Song of Songs (traditionally read allegorically of God/Christ and his people)"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Israel as the wife of YHWH: in the Old Testament and in Jewish interpretation, the marriage metaphor refers to the covenant between God and Israel, with the exodus/Sinai as betrothal and idolatry as adultery. Christian interpreters treat this as the foundation the New Testament imagery develops.","basis":["Hosea 1-3","Jeremiah 2:2; 31:32","Isaiah 54:5-6; 62:5","Ezekiel 16; 23"],"prominence":"dominant"},{"meaning":"The bride as the New Jerusalem, understood primarily as the eschatological city/dwelling of God (a place or renewed creation) rather than, or in addition to, the people themselves.","basis":["Revelation 21:2","Revelation 21:9-10"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Mystical/individual reading: the bride represents the individual soul in loving union with God or Christ, a tradition especially developed in allegorical exegesis of the Song of Songs (Origen, Bernard of Clairvaux, John of the Cross, Teresa of Avila).","basis":["Song of Songs (allegorical exegesis)","2 Corinthians 11:2 applied individually"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Dispensationalist distinction: the bride is specifically the New Testament Church, sharply distinguished from Israel; Israel is portrayed as the (restored) wife of YHWH while the Church is the bride of Christ, so the two images refer to different peoples.","basis":["Ephesians 5:22-33","Revelation 19:7-9 contrasted with Hosea 2 and Isaiah 54"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"The bride as a select subset of believers rather than all the redeemed — e.g., an especially faithful 'overcomer' class, or in Jehovah's Witnesses' teaching the 144,000 anointed who reign with Christ.","basis":["Revelation 14:1-5","Revelation 19:7-8 read restrictively"],"prominence":"rare"},{"meaning":"Marian reading: Mary as type or embodiment of the Church-bride (and of the New Eve), found in some Catholic and Orthodox theology and exegesis.","basis":["Revelation 12 read Marially alongside Revelation 21","John 2:1-11 and John 19:26-27 in typological readings"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Sacramental/creational reading: human marriage itself is the symbol — earthly marriage is an icon or sacrament pointing to Christ's union with the Church, grounding a theology of matrimony rather than only ecclesiology.","basis":["Genesis 2:24 with Ephesians 5:31-32","Matthew 19:4-6"],"prominence":"common"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"This is one of the most stable and widely recognized symbols in Christian interpretation across Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant traditions: the bride = the Church (people of God) united to Christ the bridegroom, rooted in the Old Testament picture of Israel as YHWH's wife. The alternatives listed are mostly refinements (who exactly the bride is, corporate vs. individual, people vs. city) rather than rejections of the core marital-covenant symbolism. Answer produced without access to the author's book, definition, or argument."}
